shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling/needs/work/storage come free from vanilla. Levels and per-level size are bought from a 146,000-cell budget; colder with altitude, richer ore and more cave with depth. Multi-level rendering, interaction and group ordering all verified in play.
body:
# As above, So below II — V2

> V1 is **DELETED**. ~59 files / ~15,600 LOC.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount × Slot)`; bands along **+z** from the deepest basement; permanently-fogged gutter between bands; `Slot = ceil((bandHeight+2)/64)×64` — **64-alignment is load-bearing**. Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 254, each just under a 64 boundary (~1-2% gutter waste).

### The one insight
`Region.Neighbors` is **topological, not spatial**. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms/temperature/vacuum; `Reachability.CanReach` works **unpatched**. **But reachability ≠ a path** — 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

### Hard 1.6 constraints
Path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell ⇒ **total stacked cells is the runtime metric** · no `PathFinder.FindPath` · `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN — cell budget = **146,000**
Player buys level COUNT and per-level DIMENSION from one budget on the advanced-config screen. `4 × 190 = 145,920` (three upper levels at full size) is what sets the figure; `2 × 254 = 130,048`, `7 × 126 = 112,896`; `5 × 190 = 182,400` and `7 × 190 = 255,360` refused (3-up-and-3-down at 190 auto-drops the size to 126 — the intended trade).
`ABMapSizeLimit` owns it: `UpperLevels`/`LowerLevels` (0-3 each), `BandCount`, `SurfaceBand = lower`, `Fits`, `MaxSize`, `MaxLevelsFor`, `StackedCells`. `ABV2.BandCount`/`SurfaceBand` are properties (were consts — the only thing pinning the mod to 3 levels).

### ⚠ THE CHOOSER UI — own the widget, don't patch the data
**`Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap of it SILENTLY FAILED in play.** Proof from a screenshot: vanilla's Small/Medium/Large group headers only render for sizes 200/250/300, so their presence meant our array was never in use. Worse, the postfix then re-snapped `GameInitData.mapSize` **every frame**, undoing every click — reported as "map sizes don't show correctly and nothing is selected".
**Now:** our own radio buttons live in our strip and write `mapSize` directly (a click sticks); every vanilla size is locked outright so there is exactly one control; the strip also shows cells-used-vs-budget and "this size affords up to N levels" so the dimension-vs-levels trade is visible *before* spending. Window grown +260px tall / ≥1000 wide via an `InitialSize` postfix — **vanilla lays its columns from the top and never consults the height, so added space is ours; never guess at free space inside another mod's dialog.**

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix → tick sweep carries the pawn → `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` **BFSes the band graph** and returns the best pair whose far band is `hops-1` from the target; chaining is free because each leg re-plans, and hops must strictly decrease or pawns ping-pong.
**Caveat:** an intermediate level must be walkable between arrival and the next staircase; sky levels are mostly impassable open air, so stacked stair towers work and scattered flights strand a pawn. **STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY — no test map has ever had a stair tower built.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING — three wrong layers before the right one
1. `FloatMenuMakerMap.GetOptions` clickPos — **wrong layer**; grouped orders never touch it.
2. Per-pawn `RCellFinder.BestOrderedGotoDestNear` prefix — fixed single orders but **fought vanilla's formation**.
3. **Correct:** `RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection ALONG the drag line (`root = start + (end-start) * j/(count-1)`). With endpoints on different bands that line runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature the user spotted ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 don't") is the proof: only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5, and the midpoint of a one-Slot drag is the impassable gutter. Fix = normalise `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band, leaving vanilla's maths untouched. **Verified fixed.**
Also: ordering never translates across bands unless `CanReach` says a route exists (otherwise a failed goto degenerates into walking toward the map edge); same-level orders snap to nearest ground within radius 8; the `BestOrderedGotoDestNear` prefix survives as a safety net for crates/hackables/single moves and requires reachability both sides.
`MultiPawnGotoController.Draw` is re-emitted with positions lifted into the view band (the drag line and destination ghosts previously drew at the pawns' real z = bottom of screen). Falls through to vanilla on any missing member or throw.

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE — `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band, returns the accumulated `drop`. **NINE systems share it:** `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2`, `ABBelowClickThrough`, `ABBelowOverlays`, `ABBelowDynamicDraw`, `ABBelowSelectionDraw`, `ABBelowMultiSelect`, `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen`, and — since the visuality pass — **`SectionLayer_ABBelowShadows` and `SectionLayer_ABBelowEdgeShadows`**.
A single `- Slot` step works on a 3-level map and breaks the instant two see-through levels stack. **This same bug has now appeared SEVEN times.** Appearances #6/#7 were the shadow layers, reported as *"shadows show on the first upper level, but not on upper 2 or 3"*: from +1 the single step lands on the opaque surface and works; from +2/+3 it lands in the OPEN AIR of the level between, which holds no edifices, so nothing casts.
**Sun-shadow subtlety:** that layer's mask is deliberately *neighbour*-based (a mountain-edge caster sits under an opaque cap and can never resolve a descent of its own), so mask and descent are now answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, which takes the **smallest** drop among the nine cells — the highest visible floor, i.e. the surface most of the surrounding view is showing.
**Still single-band:** the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw` (motes, fire).
Also: the **dirty mirror** now invalidates EVERY band above, not one — levels 2+ held stale bakes and never learned the ground changed ("mineables disappear on floor 2/3"; nothing was mis-drawn, nobody had invalidated the mesh).

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION — verified in play
**⚠ FOUR REJECTED ATTEMPTS — do not revisit:** force-linked wall masks (flat mask-15) · high-queue cover (erased overhanging sprites) · wall-sprite suppression (broke legibility; ore → glyphs) · theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Vanilla sprites always draw; redundant outlines are a GENERATION problem. Despeckle (majority filter; **wall dissolves only at 7+ open neighbours** — at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge, which is why plateau edges stopped reading as mountain edges) · one central fog hole · five-terrain plateau palette · cliff faces (`CliffFaceDepth 2`, `FaceDarkest 0.42`) · alpine pass (shallow-only tarns with a per-cell 6-cell edge rule, rim scree via `"Chunk"+defName`, exposure-thinned flora).
**Cross-band decoration:** `EmitMassSilhouetteAt` + static `EmitMeadowFadeAt` emit lip, corner fillers, cliff shading and meadow fades into ANY layer at a z offset, so a mountain seen from 2-3 levels up matches the one you stand on. Diagnosed from a below-layer report showing substituted rough stone and **no edge material at all** — nothing failed to print; the decoration lived in the other band's mesh.
**Ore glyph bug:** ore defs have no `naturalTerrain` (`TerrainDefGenerator_Stone` skips `isResourceRock`) ⇒ a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole **atlas sheet** per cell. `IsHostStone()` gate + fallback deleted.

# 6b. ⚠ WATER — `ABWaterV2.cs`. **1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect**
The single fact that explains most water bugs: `SectionLayer_Watergen` renders `TerrainDef.waterDepthMaterial` into the **WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's** render texture (its own Unity layer, not the map mesh), and the visible `Map/TerrainWater` material then samples that texture (`_WaterOutputTex`) **at its own screen position**. Water is therefore not self-contained geometry — printing the water material where the depth pass never wrote yields **nothing at all**.

- **Water vanished when seen from any upper level.** Half of a two-pass effect was missing: the below layer printed water's visible material, and nothing put matching depth geometry into the subcamera at the translated position. Fixed by `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` — mirrors vanilla's Watergen (`waterDepthMaterial`, plus the water-to-water edge fans that make shorelines gradient), descends via `TryResolveVisibleBelow`, and **overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`**. `SectionLayer_Watergen` is `internal` and cannot be subclassed. Bisect toggle: *below water depth*.
- **"Water always goes vertical, even in lakes."** `WaterInfo.SetTextures` publishes `_MapSize` as the map's REAL size = the whole stack (126×896 at seven levels), so anything the shader UVs by `worldPos.xz / _MapSize` is stretched by the band count along z. A **texture-scale artefact, not a flow-direction one** — which is exactly why it was uniform on every water cell including still lakes. Fixed by republishing `_MapSize` as one `Slot` (128 against a 126 band ≈ square).
- **Making the flow lookup follow:** the offset texture is addressed by that same `_MapSize`, so with `_MapSize.y = Slot` the address becomes `band + local/Slot` > 1. Solved with a **band-FOLDED flow texture whose `wrapMode` is `Repeat`** — wrap is *sampler state*, so a sample at y = 3.4 returns the row at 0.4 with **no cooperation from a shader we cannot read** (it lives in an asset bundle). Folding all bands onto one Slot's rows is what makes one texture correct for all of them, and is harmless because rivers only exist on the surface band. Cached per-Map in a CWT and explicitly `Destroy`ed on `MapRemoved` (Unity textures are not GC'd with their owner). Vanilla's own neighbour average is reproduced with its centre-cell/neighbour-cell typo **fixed**.
- **Rivers "did not generate".** They generated perfectly — three levels up. `TileMutatorWorker_River.GetRiverCenter` picks `Rand.Range(0.3f,0.7f) × map.Size.z`, which on a banded map is a fraction of the whole STACK: at seven levels that is z 268-627 while the surface band is z 384-510, so most rolls carved the river through a SKY band and the post-generation carve erased it. Fixed by remapping the anchor's z into the surface band (preserving the *roll*, not the absolute z) — patched on `GetRiverCenter`, **not** on `Init`, because Init consumes the centre immediately to build the bend noise and edge nodes. The delta/confluence/headwater/island variants inherit it, so one patch covers the family. **`TileMutatorWorker_Lake.GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first one** — `River.Init` *prefers* an existing `waterInfo.lakeCenter` over its own roll.
- **Why the band square makes this work:** the band is 126×126 out of 126×896, so a line through a re-anchored centre crosses it exactly as it would cross an ordinary map of that size, and the bend noise peaks at the segment midpoint = the anchor, i.e. inside the band.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Sky temp `-4°C × level` (compounds) · basement flat -6 · ore `×(1+0.45×(depth-1))`, cave openness `×(1+0.35×(depth-1))`, both applied AFTER the settings clamp so the slider is the level-1 baseline · mountains taper upward for free (each sky level projects from the band below, ascending generation order).
**Snow line:** generation-time snow seeding was **REMOVED** (user call — a pre-frozen top level made the most expensive level read as a different biome instead of higher ground). Nothing was lost: vanilla accumulates and melts snow per-CELL temperature, and the per-level temperature offset already makes high levels cold, so high ground still collects real snowfall, holds it after the surface thaws, and the line still moves seasonally — earned rather than painted on at t=0.

# 8. CAMERA
`freeCameraPan` REMOVED. `ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by **level**, calibrated on a 126 band: `panMargin 63.5` for +1/+3, **`maxZoom` left DERIVED** (measured 60.0 was just where the camera stopped; derive is 63.0 and an absolute would mis-scale a 190 band, where derive is 95). `Dialog_ABCameraCalibration` opens with the clamp UNLOCKED — **a calibration tool must suspend the limit it calibrates.** Clamp now bails while `Scribe` is active or state isn't `Playing` (fixed an NRE in `RectOfBand` during load-in: the camera runs every frame through a load and `ConstructComponents()` makes an empty component first).

# 9. ⚠ GENERATION COST — the top open item, now measured
| Config | Cells | Carve | Things destroyed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 × 190 | 109,440 | 5.0 s | 14,971 |
| 4 × 126 | 64,512 | 3.0 s | 24,490 |
| 7 × 126 | 112,896 | 30.4 s | 62,686 |
| **4 × 190** | **145,920** | **20.4 s** | **79,706** |
**`Sky clear` is 20.1 s of that 20.4 s — 98.6%** (6285 / 8138 / 5701 ms per band), and **`0 rocks spawned`**: every one of the 79,706 destroyed things is vanilla content generated into doomed sky bands and immediately deleted. 2.26× the cells of 4×126 produced **6.8×** the time — superlinear, because `ListerThings.Remove` is linear so cost goes ~with the SQUARE of thing count. My 10-15 s estimate was low; measure this system, never extrapolate.
**THE FIX — extend the doomed-band genstep skip.** Precedent: `Patch_WildPlantSpawner_ABSkipDoomedBands` took generation 16.9 s → 4.2 s by simply not spawning into bands the carve erases. Targets in cost order from the 4×190 profile: `RocksFromGrid` (831 ms, biggest thing-count contributor), `Terrain`, `Plants`, `RockChunks`, `ScatterShrines`, `ScatterRuinsSimple`, `CaveHives`, `MutatorPostElevationFertility`. Attacks both halves: less generated AND a smaller lister so remaining destroys are cheap.
**HARD CONSTRAINT: per-cell gensteps scope safely; `map.Area`-count scatterers do NOT** — they would dump their whole quota into the surface band. `ScatterShrines`/`ScatterRuinsSimple` are prime suspects and must be audited individually, not blanket-patched.
**Also do not blanket-skip the water mutators** — §6b depends on them running, just anchored correctly.

# 10. RUNTIME PERF — 59.6 fps @96 pawns, mod ≈2% frame. All rendering is bake-time section-mesh geometry.

# 11. VERTICAL LINKS — elevator SHIPPED, **untested**. Full-mesh 2×2; mesh is O(n²) in band count (7 levels = 21 pairs). Known: `Carry` latent hole.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
band info · **below layer report** (submesh dump — cracked the flat-mountain bug; use it BEFORE theorising) · below pawn report (DRAW/SKIP + reason) · **water report** (per-band water/withDepthMat/baseRiver census + riverGraph + flow map + published `_MapSize` — separates "the river never generated" from "the river generated three levels up and was carved") · transit health · stuck probe · transit logging · lighting/shader/biome reports · bisect toggles (click-through, below multi-select, below terrain/things/air-mask/lighting, **below water depth**, **band water globals**) · ABGenProfile · camera calibration · `CliffFaceDepth`.
The two water toggles exist because the water shader is in an **asset bundle and cannot be read** — A/B-ing `_MapSize` live is the only honest test of what the shader UVs its surface by.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **Doomed-band genstep scoping pass** (§9) — top priority; measurable before/after on 4×190.
2. **Compat, agreed and specced, not yet written:**
   - **Map Preview** (`m00nl1ght.MapPreview`) — it never sees our banding at all: `MapPreviewRequest` runs only `ElevationFertility`/`Terrain`/`MutatorPost*` on its own map, **never through `MapGenerator.GenerateMap`**, sized from `world.info.initialMapSize` which we deliberately keep at the SURFACE size. So it previews a normal 126×126 map while the real surface band is a horizontal slice at z 384-510 of a 126×896 one — completely different noise. Fix = force the preview to generate at the inflated height, then crop the texture to the surface band. Must be **reflection-only**: it is a Lunar component, dynamically loaded. Useful hooks found: `MapPreviewAPI.IsGeneratingPreview`, `MapSizeUtility.MapSizeOverride`, `MapPreviewRequest.TextureSize`.
   - **Dubs Mint Minimap** (`dubwise.dubsmintminimap`) — should show only the active level. Fully patchable but the biggest job (~250 LOC): everything keys off `map.Size` and one static `MapTexture`, and band-scoping needs `UpdateMapTex` **plus** the coordinate mapping in `Minimap`/`DrawAllPawns`/`DrawFires`/`DrawProjectiles`/`DrawPings`/`DrawCam`, which all lerp against `map.Size.z`. Note it also draws a 126×896 texture through `DrawTextureFitted(..., texProportions: 1f)`, so today the whole stack is squashed into a square.
3. **Never exercised in play:** multi-hop stair router (needs a stair tower), elevator, reload fix (menu-load, load-while-playing, double cycle, now also at 7 bands).
4. Realtime-things pass still single-band (motes/fire >1 level down).
5. Selection bracket **drifts upward as you zoom out** — zoom-dependence means something in that path mixes world and screen space; our offset is in world units.
6. **Option E — waterfalls**: now less risky than it was, since below-view water is proven by §6b. Tarns never de-risked it (same-band water).
7. COMBAT never verified · Option C (stepped mesa) parked · vertical conduit · compat audit incl. Better Mountains co-load · transplant (coastline slicing — **river slicing is now fixed by anchoring, §6b**) · **store page still says three levels**.

# 14. LESSONS (telegraphic)
**Run the diagnostic before the third theory** — two wrong guesses cost two cycles; the submesh dump answered it instantly · **an odd/even or count-dependent symptom is arithmetic — find the formula** · **a UNIFORM symptom is a scale/constant, a PATCHY one is data** (that alone separated stretched `_MapSize` from a ghost flow field) · **when a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes** — 1.6 water is two, and only one of them was ported · **wrap mode is sampler state, so `Repeat` can fix UV addressing inside a shader you cannot read** · measure, don't extrapolate (Option D estimate wrong 100× low; 4×190 carve wrong 2× low) · **a single-step assumption survives until the data has two steps — grep `X + 1`, `== N`, every `- Slot`; it has now bitten SEVEN times** · **generation anchors picked as a fraction of `map.Size.z` all land in the wrong band — audit every one** · **patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it, when the storer consumes it immediately** · **own the widget instead of patching the data it reads; `static readonly` reflection writes fail silently** · **never fight the player's input every frame** · never hide sprites that carry gameplay information · visual noise in generated content is a GENERATION bug · ore defs have no naturalTerrain · a `Graphic_Linked` base material is the whole ATLAS SHEET · **"can't happen" fallbacks are what the player photographs** · enforce spatial rules PER CELL, not seed+radius · key authored tables by stable semantics (level), not index · **budget the real cost, don't cap a proxy** · a per-leg re-planning router needs only the FIRST HOP of a BFS · **normalise the anchor, don't rewrite each member — leave vanilla's formation maths alone** · never a queue-above-cutout cover · clip geometry to cells you own · vertex colour on terrain dims the real texture · statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak — CWT · **Unity textures are not GC'd with their owner — `Destroy` them on `MapRemoved`** · never cache comps while Scribe active · FinalizeInit = worker thread · altitude ≠ draw order but IS the cutout depth tiebreaker · `material.shader =` resets renderQueue · static Unity-asset fields need `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]` · `SectionLayer` subclasses are **auto-discovered** by `Section`'s ctor — no registration · when art is in asset bundles, playtest screenshots are a legitimate mockup source.

## TESTING RULE
`isolated=true`. Companions: `astryl.Circinus` + `astryl.ModernDevTools` + `BiomesTeam.BiomesCaverns` + `BiomesTeam.CoreFramework` — **drop them for isolation runs when a bug might not be ours** (that discriminator proved the group-order bug WAS ours). Multi-level tests need `quicktest=false` (levels are chosen on the map-size screen). Reload tests need load-while-playing. **Water/river tests need a tile that actually has a river or lake landmark** — pick one on the world map deliberately, and take a fresh colony (the anchoring fix is generation-time only).
